Cleanup applied in working tree; unit and verify suites identical to baseline. Commit pending user approval per conservative profile.

RFC 9773 ARI implemented: acme/ari.lisp (certID, RFC3339 parsing, client-renewal-info, renewal-due-p), replaces field in client-new-order with retry-without fallback, adaptive renewal default in acme-acceptor (ARI window, else 1/3 lifetime; explicit :renewal-days keeps fixed behavior). 34 new tests incl. RFC Appendix A vector, all green; existing retry suite and unit tests unchanged.

GREASE value now prepended to signature_algorithms (client.lisp), stable across CH1/CH2 like other GREASE values. GREASE-Client-TLS13 passes on BoringSSL ebd832c39; full suite vs CI-pinned 606d3a3 shows zero regressions (2211 failures, identical to baseline); unit tests identical; live connect to example.com works. Also fixed Makefile so pure-tls-shim is .PHONY (stale shim masked the first verification attempt).

Added 'make acme-tests' target (runs retry + ARI suites, verified locally: 63/63 pass, exit 0, wired into all-tests) and CI steps in test.yml for all three OS after offline tests; added missing cl-json to the ocicl install lists. YAML validated locally; actual CI run pending next push.

Landed via fade's PR #24, merged locally as d64dd38 (GitHub API was erroring on the merge endpoint; merged the fetched branch and pushed instead). Conflicts with the local whittle/docstring work resolved in the merge commit: kept the keyword signature and PR guard comments, kept the whittle deletions and the accurate CRL/OCSP docstring wording. Full unit, verify, and acme suites green on the merged tree.
1.14.0 released: commit 1aeded2 pushed, Tests green (run 34751630757), tag v1.14.0 pushed, Release workflow succeeded (run 34751911843), GitHub release published

Reviewed. No attacker path: the message_hash(CH1)||HRR||CH2 transcript plus Finished binds everything both sides agree on, and key-schedule-init reads the freshly-computed local accepted-psk, never the sticky struct slot, so an unauthenticated PSK can never reach key derivation. Every CH1/CH2 divergence traced (cipher suite, key_share group, SNI, ALPN, PSK) ends in an abort or an agreed-but-cosmetically-wrong ServerHello. Spun out 3 non-security bugs: sticky PSK state across HRR, SNI callback never running with a default cert, and two missing RFC 8446 MUST-aborts.

Reviewed both native verifiers in full. One security finding filed (native dispatch bypasses the no-trusted-roots fail-closed guard; :replace with NIL roots falls back to the OS store). Three non-security bugs spun out: macOS Boolean return declared as 4-byte CFFI :boolean, native failure messages silently discarded via wrong condition initargs, and Windows :extend likely not extending trust. Checked and clean: CFFI pointer lifetimes and release ordering in both files (no double-free or leak found on any error branch - %create-certificate-array's ownership handoff and windows' pointer-eq guard on hcert are both correct), SecTrustEvaluateWithError is the modern fail-closed API, EKU purpose is enforced before the native dispatch so it applies on all platforms, and Win32 BOOL is correctly sized. Note: the :now argument is silently ignored on both native paths.

Reviewed src/crypto/hpke.lisp in full against RFC 9180 and the ECH crypto helpers in src/handshake/ech.lisp. No security findings. Verified correct: LabeledExtract/LabeledExpand construction, DHKEM kem_context = enc||pkR, the base-mode key schedule (psk_id_hash / info_hash / ks_context / secret) matches s5.1 exactly, hpke-compute-nonce XORs the 64-bit seq into the low 8 bytes of the 12-byte base nonce correctly, the ECH accept-confirmation comparison uses constant-time-equal, and the ServerHello.random[24..31] offset (30..38 in the serialized message) is right. Three non-security bugs spun out: missing RFC 9180 s7.1.4 all-zero DH check, accept confirmation hardcoded to SHA-256 while SHA-384 suites are offered, and CL:RANDOM in GREASE ECH. Note server-side ECH is not implemented, so hpke decap has no attacker-facing caller.

Reviewed both files. One security finding filed: ML-DSA-65 verification measured at 77ms (schoolbook O(n^2), no optimize declarations), which an unbounded Certificate message turns into ~315 CPU-seconds per connection. Two conformance bugs spun out (ML-DSA decode-hints missing FIPS 204 Alg 15 strictly-increasing and zero-padding checks; ML-KEM missing the FIPS 203 s7.2 ek modulus check) plus a portability bead on the constant-time assumptions. KILLED two speculative crypto candidates by disassembly rather than shipping them: the KyberSlash-shaped division in compress-coeff compiles to MUL+SAR with no DIV, and the secret-dependent message-bit branch in k-pke-decrypt compiles to CMOV with no jumps. Verified correct: FIPS 203 s7.3 implicit rejection in decaps, ct-cond-sub-q's mask over its full input range, the X25519MLKEM768 combiner order (ML-KEM first) and its 1088/1120/1184/1216 length checks at the TLS layer. ML-DSA signing is unreachable - ml-dsa-65-sign has no caller and load-private-key cannot produce an ML-DSA key - so ML-DSA is verification-only and operates purely on public data.

Fixed: added +asn1-max-depth+ (64) and threaded a depth counter through parse-der-node/parse-der-contents in src/x509/asn1.lisp; nesting past the cap now signals tls-decode-error. Regression tests der-nesting-depth-is-bounded and certificate-nesting-depth-is-bounded added to test/security-regression-tests.lisp, including the 30000-deep payload that previously killed the image. Security regression suite: 65 checks, 100% pass.

Fixed: rewrote tls-stream-fill-buffer (src/streams.lisp) from self-recursion to an iterative LOOP, so the frame count is flat regardless of record count. Added +max-consecutive-handshake-records+ (64) with a tls-stream-handshake-record-count slot that resets when a message completes or app data arrives, bounding a no-progress dribble without penalising long-lived connections. Unknown post-handshake message types now send unexpected_message and error per RFC 8446 s4.6 instead of being silently ignored. Regression tests post-handshake-record-dribble-is-bounded (20000 records, previously fatal at ~11250) and post-handshake-unknown-message-is-rejected added. Full unit suite green including OpenSSL resumption interop.

Fixed: *max-certificate-list-size* now defaults to 102400 (matching OpenSSL's SSL_CTX_set_max_cert_list default) instead of 0/unlimited, so a Certificate message is bounded at 100KB rather than the 16MB uint24 protocol maximum. Test certificate-list-size-has-a-bounded-default added. Note this is a mitigation for pure-tls-yg4 and pure-tls-8m4, not the fix for either.

Fixed. Added an NTT-based polynomial multiply to src/crypto/ml-dsa.lisp (ml-dsa-ntt!, ml-dsa-intt!, ml-dsa-poly-mul-ntt, *ml-dsa-zetas* derived at load time from root 1753) and pointed ml-dsa-matrix-vector-mul and ml-dsa-scalar-poly-mul at it. Schoolbook retained as the reference.

MEASURED END TO END: ml-dsa-65-verify 77ms -> 8.80ms (8.75x). NOT the 36x my polynomial-multiply micro-benchmark suggested - that only covered the 36 multiplies (77ms -> 1.35ms). Profiling the rest: expand-a 2.00ms, decode/use-hint/encode paths ~5.5ms.

With pure-tls-cjm bounding a Certificate message to 100KB (~18 ML-DSA certs), the attack goes from ~315 CPU-seconds per connection to ~0.16 CPU-seconds - a ~2000x reduction, comparable to an RSA-4096 chain. Security objective met.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERION NOT MET: I asked for '<1ms' and delivered 8.8ms. The remaining cost is ordinary un-optimised bit-manipulation, not the O(n^2) defect; filed as a separate performance bead.

Verified with new differential tests ml-dsa-ntt-matches-schoolbook (25 pseudo-random trials plus zero/identity/q-1 edge cases, asserting the NTT and schoolbook products are identical) and ml-dsa-ntt-roundtrips. This suite has no FIPS 204 KATs, so the schoolbook reference IS the verification. ML-DSA suite 63 checks green; full unit suite 13/13 clean.

Fixed - and it turned out to be TWO defects, which is why RSA-PSS was entirely non-functional rather than merely wrong.
(1) src/x509/verify.lisp and src/x509/crl.lisp now pass raw tbs to ironclad:verify-signature :pss instead of (digest-sequence hash-algo tbs); ironclad's pss-verify hashes the message itself. Dropped the :salt-length argument, which pss-verify does not accept (it infers it).
(2) Discovered while testing: the bare digest OIDs 2.16.840.1.101.3.4.2.{1,2,3,4} and 1.3.14.3.2.26 were absent from *well-known-oids*, so parse-rsa-pss-params could not resolve hashAlgorithm and handed ironclad a raw OID list -> 'not a supported digest'. Added them to src/x509/asn1.lisp.
Verified end to end against real OpenSSL-generated RSA-PSS certificates (SHA-256/saltlen 32 and SHA-384/saltlen 48), added as fixtures test/certs/rsa-pss-selfsigned.pem and rsa-pss-sha384-selfsigned.pem. Tests rsa-pss-certificate-signature-verifies AND rsa-pss-certificate-signature-rejects-tampering (a flipped tbs byte must still fail, so the fix is not a blanket accept). Security regression suite 78 checks green.

Fixed, but NOT the way the design section proposed. Moving the (unless trusted-roots ...) guard above the native dispatches would have broken the primary Windows client path: *use-windows-certificate-store* defaults to T precisely so the OS decides, and on a host without a Git-for-Windows CA bundle load-system-trust-store legitimately yields an empty store, so NIL roots there mean 'use the OS store' by design. A blanket error would reject working configurations.

Fixed instead at the two places where NIL is unambiguous:
 - src/handshake/server.lisp process-client-certificate-verify now requires (and trust-store (trust-store-certificates trust-store)) under +verify-required+, and skips chain verification for an empty store rather than calling verify-certificate-chain with NIL roots. This closes the reachable mTLS path.
 - Client paths were already covered: make-tls-context errors when :ca-file/:ca-directory yield zero certificates (src/context.lisp).
Documented the overloaded meaning of NIL trusted-roots at the native dispatch in src/x509/verify.lisp, with an explicit warning that new callers must make the same check rather than assuming the function fails closed.

Test empty-trust-store-is-not-a-usable-anchor-set added, including the make-trust-store-from-directory behaviour that makes an empty store reachable by ordinary misconfiguration. Full suite 13/13 clean.

Still unverified on a real macOS/Windows host - I have neither. The reachability argument and the fix are both static.

Fixed: compat/api.lisp no longer silently discards security-relevant cl+ssl options. make-context now signals ssl-error for :verify-callback (the cl+ssl pinning/custom-policy hook, which pure-tls has no equivalent for) and for :pem-password-callback / :private-key-password. make-ssl-client-stream signals for :certificate / :key with a pointer to pure-tls:make-tls-client-stream's :client-certificate / :client-key. Options that are genuinely meaningless for a TLS-1.3-only stack (method, disabled-protocols, options, min-proto-version, session-cache-mode, cipher-list) still no-op silently, and that distinction is now documented in the docstring. Verified: verify-callback and private-key-password are refused, plain make-context still works.

Fixed: added a provider-supplied-certificate slot to server-handshake, set when the certificate-provider returns a chain during THIS ClientHello and cleared at the top of each one. The sni-callback is now gated on that instead of (null certificate-chain), which was also true whenever a default :certificate was configured. Verified the new test sni-callback-runs-when-default-certificate-configured FAILS against the old gate and passes with the fix, so it is a real regression guard rather than a tautology. Full suite 13/13 clean.

Fixed: *session-ticket-cache-lock* now holds a real bt:make-lock (was defvar'd NIL and never used) and all three accessors - session-ticket-cache-get, -put, -clear - hold it. Chose an explicit lock over :synchronized T because -get does a read-then-remhash that must be atomic as a unit. Full suite green including resumption interop.

Fixed: replaced CL:RANDOM with CSPRNG draws at all three sites. src/handshake/ech.lisp generate-grease-ech-extension now derives both config-id and the payload length from random-bytes (the enc/payload bytes already did). acme/challenges.lisp generate-placeholder-certificate and generate-validation-certificate now build the 64-bit serial from ironclad:random-data, which also removes the SBCL thread-safety hazard of the shared global *random-state*. Verified a generated placeholder certificate still parses with a full-width serial.

Fixed: all four sites (3 in src/x509/macos-verify.lisp, 1 in src/x509/windows-verify.lisp) now pass :message (format nil ...) instead of the :format-control/:format-arguments initargs that tls-certificate-error does not accept. SBCL silently discarded those initargs, so every native verification failure reported as a bare 'TLS certificate error' with the CFError description or decoded Windows status computed and thrown away.

Fixed: deleted verify-peer-certificate and trust-store-find-issuer from src/x509/verify.lisp, replacing them with a comment recording why (DN-only matching, no signature verification) and pointing callers at verify-certificate-chain. Confirmed neither was exported and neither had any caller before removal. Builds clean; full suite green.

Fixed: .github/workflows/release.yml now declares permissions: contents: write instead of write-all, and pins ncipollo/release-action to commit 339a81892b84b4eeb0f6e744e4574d79d0d9b8dd (v1.21.0, resolved via the GitHub API) rather than the mutable v1 tag. Also added a guard rejecting any tag whose version is not vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, closing the bodyFile path-traversal noted in the report. YAML validated.

Fixed: decode-hints (src/crypto/ml-dsa.lisp) now enforces all three FIPS 204 Algorithm 15 checks. Added step 8 (indices strictly increasing within each polynomial's run) and step 10 (every unused index slot must be zero); step 6 (counts non-decreasing, bounded by omega) was already present. Test ml-dsa-hint-decoding-is-canonical covers all five rejection cases plus the well-formed baseline.

Fixed: added ml-kem-check-encapsulation-key implementing the FIPS 203 S7.2 length + modulus check (every 12-bit coefficient < q), called from ml-kem-768-encaps. Also added self-contained length assertions to ml-kem-768-decaps (ciphertext and dk), hybrid-compute-shared-secret and hybrid-server-encaps, so those entry points no longer depend on the TLS layer's key_share check for memory safety.

Fixed: added hpke-check-x25519-key (RFC 7748 S5 32-byte length) and hpke-check-dh-secret (RFC 9180 S7.1.4 all-zero rejection) to src/crypto/hpke.lisp, applied on BOTH hpke-x25519-encap and hpke-x25519-decap. Mirrors the check x25519-compute-shared-secret already makes on the TLS key-exchange path, so decap is correct in advance of server-side ECH landing.

Fixed: compute-ech-accept-confirmation now takes the negotiated cipher suite and derives hash-len, HKDF-Extract and HKDF-Expand-Label from cipher-suite-digest instead of hardcoding SHA-256; the caller in src/handshake/client.lisp likewise computes the ECH transcript hash with the negotiated digest. ECH is no longer silently treated as rejected on every SHA-384 handshake. Note the hpke-key-schedule kdf-id footgun mentioned in this bead remains - it is still ignored, but ech-cipher-suite-supported-p refuses any kdf-id other than HKDF-SHA256, so it is unreachable; left as-is rather than widening scope.

Fixed: psk-accepted / accepted-psk / selected-psk-index are now set UNCONDITIONALLY from each ClientHello's local result in process-client-hello, and cleared when no PSK was accepted. Previously they were only ever set, so after a HelloRetryRequest a CH2 that dropped its PSK left CH1's values in place and generate-server-hello advertised an acceptance the key schedule never made. Validated by the full BoringSSL TLS 1.3 suite: zero new failures, and AlwaysSelectPSKIdentity-TLS13 now PASSES (it was in the committed baseline as failing).

Both fixed.
(1) Client: src/handshake/client.lisp process-server-hello now sends illegal_parameter and errors when the server includes pre_shared_key but no PSK was offered, per RFC 8446 s4.1.3, instead of silently dropping the extension.
(2) Server: src/handshake/server.lisp now rejects a second ClientHello whose key_share group differs from the group named in the HelloRetryRequest, per RFC 8446 s4.1.4.
Confirmed by the BoringSSL suite: AlwaysSelectPSKIdentity-TLS13 moved from the failing baseline to passing, zero new failures.

Fixed: SecTrustEvaluateWithError and CFStringGetCString are now declared (:boolean :uint8) rather than bare :boolean, which CFFI reads as its default 4-byte :int base type. CoreFoundation's Boolean is 'typedef unsigned char'. Also made the two Boolean ARGUMENT declarations (SecPolicyCreateSSL's server, SecTrustSetAnchorCertificatesOnly's anchors-only) consistent, though argument direction was always harmless.
VERIFICATION LIMIT: macos-verify.lisp is :if-feature gated and is not compiled on this Linux host, so the unit suite does not exercise it. I force-compiled it with :darwin pushed onto *features* - CFFI accepts the (:boolean :uint8) syntax and the file compiles with no warnings or failures - but this has NOT been run against a real Security.framework.

Fixed: added %write-private-temp-file, which creates the file with sb-posix:open and mode #o600 AT CREATION plus O_CREAT|O_EXCL - no umask window, and O_EXCL refuses to follow a pre-placed symlink. Filenames now carry 128 bits of CSPRNG entropy (%unpredictable-temp-name) so the path cannot be predicted in the first place. Applied to both the validation key and the *acme-debug* copy. Non-SBCL falls back to :if-exists :error with an explicit warning. Verified: generated key file is mode 600 with a random name, and writing to a pre-placed symlink is refused with SYSCALL-ERROR leaving the target file untouched. Kept start-tls-alpn-server rather than deleting it - the pebble integration test uses it and securing the write is the smaller change.

Fixed by enforcing, not removing. Added *default-verify-depth* (100) in src/constants.lisp; verify-certificate-chain now takes :max-depth (defaulting to it) and rejects a chain longer than the limit BEFORE any signature verification - which is the point, since per-link verification runs before the trust-anchor check. make-tls-client-stream and make-tls-server-stream bind *default-verify-depth* from the context's verify-depth for the duration of the handshake, so the context slot (and cl+ssl's :verify-depth) now actually does something. Test verify-depth-limits-chain-length added. Full unit suite clean; BoringSSL suite still 0 new failures / 2 newly passing.

All six adjudicated; five fixed, one documented.
1. :now ignored on native paths -> DOCUMENTED in verify-certificate-chain's docstring (the OS backends have no API to override their clock, so this cannot be fixed, only stated).
2. ensure-directory-with-mode's invalid (declare ...) in non-declaration position -> FIXED: moved to (declare (ignorable mode)) at the head of the body; the #-sbcl branch no longer emits an illegal form.
3. parse-ed25519/ed448-private-key hardcoded (subseq key-bytes 2) -> FIXED: added %unwrap-curve-private-key, which parses the RFC 8410 CurvePrivateKey OCTET STRING properly instead of assuming a one-byte length. Ed25519/Ed448 key-loading tests still pass.
4. load-certificate-chain silently skipping unparseable certificates -> FIXED: counts skips and emits a summary warning naming the count and the trust-store consequence, in addition to the existing per-certificate warning.
5. Unbounded *crl-cache* keyed by peer-supplied CDP URIs -> FIXED: added *crl-cache-max-entries* (256); the cache is cleared when the cap is reached.
6. hpke-increment-seq comparing against 2^96 while the slot is (unsigned-byte 64) -> FIXED: bound is now (min 64 (* 8 Nn)) so the explicit check runs before the struct type check.
Full unit suite 13/13 clean.

Addressed via option (b): the assumption is now explicit and enforced by a test.
Extracted the secret-dependent message-bit decode out of k-pke-decrypt into ml-kem-decode-message-bit (no arithmetic change) so its codegen can be asserted on. Added two guards to test/crypto-tests.lisp, gated #+(and sbcl x86-64):
 - ml-kem-compress-coeff-has-no-hardware-divide: fails if DIV/IDIV appears (the KyberSlash shape) and asserts the multiply that replaces it is present.
 - ml-kem-message-bit-decode-is-branch-free: fails on any conditional jump and asserts CMOV is present.
Verified the branch detector actually fires: it reports 0 conditional jumps for ml-kem-decode-message-bit and 5 for poly-compress (which has a loop), so the guard can fail rather than passing vacuously.
Chose this over rewriting both expressions branch-free by hand (option a): hand-written multiply-shift division in a crypto primitive carries real arithmetic-bug risk, there is no reference implementation to difference compress-coeff against, and the compiler already produces the right code on this platform. A port to another backend will now fail loudly instead of silently regressing.

All seven leads adjudicated; all seven fixed.
1. parse-der-contents now requires a child to end exactly at its parent's declared length (was: a nested node could overrun the parent while staying in-buffer). Test der-child-may-not-overrun-parent.
2. known-certificate-extension-p is now (and oid (symbolp oid)) - (symbolp NIL) is T, so a critical extension with a zero-length OID was treated as known and accepted.
3. decode-der-oid rewritten: the first subidentifier is now decoded as a full base-128 value (OIDs like 2.100.3 were mis-decoded by reading only bytes[0]), and non-minimal subidentifiers (leading 0x80) and unterminated ones are rejected, so one OID no longer has many valid encodings. Test der-oid-decoding-is-strict-and-complete.
4. check-certificate-revocation now applies crl-valid-p to a freshly fetched CRL (get-cached-crl already did), closing the replay of an old-but-validly-signed CRL over the plaintext HTTP fetch.
5. pool-release now wipes every tier before returning a buffer to the process-global pool, not just the large one.
6. supported_versions / supported_groups / signature_algorithms now decode through decode-uint16-list, which signals tls-decode-error on an odd length instead of running AREF off the end with a raw SB-INT:INVALID-ARRAY-INDEX-ERROR that escaped the handshake's TLS-* handlers. Test uint16-extension-lists-reject-odd-length.
7. Removed the contradictory (declare (ignore hs)) in try-accept-psk.
Validation: unit suite 13/13 clean, ACME suites 29+34 checks clean, BoringSSL 0 new failures / 2 newly passing.

NOT A BUG - my original claim was wrong, corrected after reading the test definition.

TLS13-Server-NoSharedCipher passes flagInts("-tls13-ciphers", [TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384]) to restrict the SHIM's server to AES-256-GCM only, while the runner's client offers AES-128-GCM and CHACHA20. The shim did not parse -tls13-ciphers (its argument loop ends in 'Skip unknown flags but continue'), so pure-tls used its own default suite list, which does share a suite with the client, and the handshake correctly succeeded. The 'unexpected success' was the shim ignoring configuration, not the server accepting a handshake it should have rejected.

Fixed anyway, and the test now PASSES: the shim honours -tls13-ciphers, :cipher-suites is plumbed through make-tls-client-stream / make-tls-server-stream (it was dead configuration on both paths), and the no-common-cipher error is renamed :NO_SHARED_CIPHER: to match the BoringSSL convention the codebase already follows.

NOT A BUG, same root cause as pure-tls-dph. The four TLS-ECH-Client-RejectUnusableConfig tests configure the client with -ech-config-list and -reject-unusable-ech-config; the shim parsed neither, so it never offered ECH at all and the runner reported 'server did not accept ECH'. Nothing was wrong with select-ech-config or the RFC 9639 handling.

The shim now declares these unimplemented so the runner skips them rather than reporting a spurious failure. Wiring real client-side ECH configuration into the shim would give genuine coverage of that code path and is worth doing; folded into the shim-coverage follow-up rather than kept open here as a phantom ECH bug.

Done. Bumped BORINGSSL_REF from 606d3a3 (2026-06-18) to 8626998 (2026-09-17) and regenerated the baseline against it.

Result: baseline 2065 -> 2062 with ZERO failures added; three removed because upstream changed the tests and they now pass (ClientHelloPadding, ClientShouldNotAllowInTLS12-Kyber, PostQuantumNotEnabledByDefaultInClients). Suite grows 7908 -> 8089 tests.

Both blockers this bead recorded are resolved:
(1) Output-format change -- both scripts now parse either format via test/boringssl-summary.sh, and refuse truncated runs.
(2) The 41 newly-failing tests -- all were the shim ignoring flags it does not parse, not pure-tls defects. 28 Compliance-fips-202609 plus cnsa1/cnsa2 now skip via check-unimplemented-features; the 13 non-FIPS were triaged individually (1 fixed and passing, 12 declared unimplemented).

Also set TEST_TIMEOUT=1800 explicitly on the CI regression step: a full run is ~750s of CPU across cores, which can exceed the 300s default on a hosted runner, and truncation is now a hard failure rather than silent partial results.
